A. Cochlear organ dissection
Fine dissection of the organ of Corti

steps.title: Prepare 1× PBS solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 8 g NaCl, 200 mg KCl, 1.44 g NaH₂PO₄·7H₂O, and 240 mg KH₂PO₄ in distilled water, adjust the volume to 1 000 mL, set pH to 7.4 with HCl, and store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 4% PFA solution
steps.instruction: Weigh 4 g paraformaldehyde powder, add to 100 mL 1× PBS, heat to ~60 °C while stirring under a chemical hood until the solution becomes transparent, cool, filter through Whatman paper, aliquot into 50 mL tubes, freeze at –20 °C, and wear appropriate PPE.

steps.title: Euthanize mouse
steps.instruction: Euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation or by inhalation of 100 % CO₂.

steps.title: Decapitate and expose temporal bones
steps.instruction: Decapitate the mouse with small scissors, then use large forceps to remove the brain on each side, exposing the temporal bones.

steps.title: Isolate bony labyrinths
steps.instruction: Under a dissecting microscope, use fine forceps to isolate the bony labyrinths from the temporal bones.

steps.title: Trim tissue and remove stapes
steps.instruction: Trim away additional tissue and remove the stapes from the oval window.

steps.title: Clear windows and fix labyrinths
steps.instruction: Use the tip of fine forceps to clear the oval and round windows and make a small hole in the apex of the cochlear spiral, then fix the bony labyrinths in 1.5 mL 4 % PFA for 5 min on ice.

steps.title: Transfer labyrinths to PBS dish
steps.instruction: Place the fixed bony labyrinths in a dissecting dish containing PBS to facilitate the next steps.

steps.title: Remove outer cartilage
steps.instruction: Using fine forceps, remove the outer cartilage to expose the cochlear duct.

steps.title: Remove stria vascularis
steps.instruction: Slowly remove the stria vascularis with fine forceps, attempting to take the whole stria in one attempt.

steps.title: Remove Reissner’s membrane
steps.instruction: Use very fine forceps to remove Reissner’s membrane, visualizing the dorsal aspect of the cochlear duct and the sensory epithelium.

steps.title: Remove tectorial membrane
steps.instruction: Use very fine forceps to remove the tectorial membrane.

steps.title: Dissect organ of Corti
steps.instruction: Use very fine forceps to remove the intact organ of Corti.

steps.title: Fix organ of Corti
steps.instruction: Fix the organ of Corti in a 48‑well plate containing 0.5 mL 4 % PFA for either 2 h at room temperature, 2 h on ice, or overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Permeabilize with Triton X‑100
steps.instruction: Transfer the organ of Corti to a new well with 0.5 mL 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in PBS (PBS‑T) for 10–20 min at room temperature; no agitation is required; handle with very fine forceps.

steps.title: Block with 10% donkey serum
steps.instruction: Incubate the tissues in 10 % normal donkey serum in PBS‑T for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Incubate the organ of Corti in primary antibodies diluted in 5 % normal donkey serum in PBS‑T overnight at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Rab11a, 1:200 (Cell Signaling Technology, cat 2413)

steps.title: Wash with PBS‑T
steps.instruction: Wash the samples with 0.5 mL PBS‑T three times, each wash lasting 1–2 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Incubate the samples in secondary antibodies diluted in 5 % normal donkey serum in PBS‑T for 2 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C; protect from light.

substeps.instruction: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti‑mouse IgG (H+L), 1:1000 (Jackson Immuno‑Research, cat 715‑545‑151)
Rhodamine Red‑X donkey anti‑mouse IgG (H+L), 1:1000 (Jackson Immuno‑Research, cat 715‑295‑151)
Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti‑mouse IgG (H+L), 1:1000 (Jackson Immuno‑Research, cat 715‑605‑151)

steps.title: Wash post‑secondary
steps.instruction: Wash the samples with PBS‑T three times, each wash 1–2 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Stain with phalloidin
steps.instruction: Incubate the tissue in phalloidin (1:1000) diluted in 5 % normal donkey serum in PBS‑T for 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Final PBS‑T washes
steps.instruction: Wash the sample with PBS‑T three times, each wash 1–2 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Place basilar membrane in PBS
steps.instruction: Gently transfer the basilar membrane into a drop of PBS placed on a microscope slide.

steps.title: Orient sample for mounting
steps.instruction: Under the microscope, use very fine forceps to orient the sample so that the apical side faces upward toward the coverslip.

steps.title: Apply mounting medium and coverslip
steps.instruction: Add a drop of mounting medium onto the basilar membrane, place one side of a coverslip at an angle against the slide to touch the outer edge of the liquid drop, then lower the coverslip gently, avoiding air bubbles.

steps.title: Remove excess medium
steps.instruction: Use an absorbent tissue or filter paper to wick away any excess mounting medium from the edges of the coverslip.

steps.title: Seal slide and store
steps.instruction: Seal the coverslip to the slide with nail polish, then store the slide at 4 °C in a dark environment until imaging.

steps.title: Check labeling intensity
steps.instruction: Inspect the sample using negative controls to assess labeling intensity and background.

steps.title: Acquire confocal images
steps.instruction: Capture all pictures using identical exposure and general settings for each fluorophore channel.

steps.title: Set microscope parameters
steps.instruction: Use a Zeiss LSM510 confocal microscope with 20–63× oil‑immersion objectives (NA 1.4) and 488‑nm and 555‑nm laser lines for excitation.

steps.title: Create maximum intensity projection
steps.instruction: Apply the Z‑projection function with the Maximum Intensity option to generate a two‑dimensional view of each image stack.

steps.title: Define cochlear positions for analysis
steps.instruction: Mark specific positions along the cochlear duct (25 %, 50 %, 75 % from the base) for regional protein comparison.

steps.title: Capture images for quantification
steps.instruction: Take images for quantifying stereocilia morphology, orientation, and cilia number as described (e.g., bundle height, bundle angle, Arl13b‑positive cilia counts).

steps.title: Analyze images with ImageJ
steps.instruction: Open images in ImageJ and perform the following analyses:

substeps.instruction: Use the straight line tool to connect the two ends of a stereocilia bundle.
Use the straight line tool to measure the shortest distance between the bundle vertex and the line connecting the ends (bundle height).
Select Analyze > Measure to record the length.
Use the angle tool to draw the bisector of the V‑shaped bundle (angles 1 and 2).
Use the angle tool to draw a horizontal reference line.
Measure the angle between the bisector and the horizontal line (angle 3).
Select Analyze > Measure to record the angle.
